queries: WITH o AS (SELECT order_id, AVG(CAST(product_quantity AS REAL)) AS avg_qty FROM Order_Items GROUP BY order_id), t AS (SELECT AVG(CAST(product_quantity AS REAL)) AS overall_avg FROM Order_Items) SELECT o.order_id, o.avg_qty AS order_avg_quantity, o.avg_qty - t.overall_avg AS diff_from_overall FROM o CROSS JOIN t WHERE t.overall_avg IS NOT NULL ORDER BY diff_from_overall DESC, o.order_id LIMIT 10

responses.sql: WITH o AS (SELECT order_id, AVG(CAST(product_quantity AS REAL)) AS avg_qty FROM Order_Items GROUP BY order_id), t AS (SELECT AVG(CAST(product_quantity AS REAL)) AS overall_avg FROM Order_Items) SELECT o.order_id, o.avg_qty AS order_avg_quantity, o.avg_qty - t.overall_avg AS diff_from_overall FROM o CROSS JOIN t WHERE t.overall_avg IS NOT NULL ORDER BY diff_from_overall DESC, o.order_id LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: product_quantity is stored as text (VARCHAR) but holds numeric values, so it is cast to a number. Missing values (NULL) are ignored by AVG.
The overall average is the average over all Order_Items rows (row-weighted), not the average of the per-order averages.
Orders whose quantities are all missing are kept, with a NULL difference. Under DESC ordering, NULLs sort last in SQLite but first in some other databases such as PostgreSQL.
Ties in the difference are broken by order_id ascending, which the request does not specify.

alternatives.interpretation: The overall average is the mean of the per-order averages, so each order counts equally.

assumptions.assumption: product_quantity is stored as text but holds numeric values, so it is cast to a number. Empty or NULL values are treated as missing and ignored by AVG. This assumes missing values are NULL rather than empty strings, since an empty string would cast to 0 in some databases.
The overall average is the average of product_quantity over all Order_Items rows, not the average of the per-order averages.
Orders with no Order_Items rows are not listed, because the request says 'for each order in Order_Items'.

alternatives.interpretation: The overall average is the mean of the per-order averages, so each order counts equally regardless of its number of items.
